entries.title: Drones buzz overhead, troops hunker underground in Ukraine's hellish Kill Zone
entries.snippet: The frontline in the Russia-Ukraine war stretches more than 700 miles and has barely moved in four years. Yet straddling this line is the Kill Zone, dominated by constantly evolving drone technology.

entries.title: FBI arrests a woman accused of spying on Taiwan leader's family for China
entries.snippet: The FBI and U.S. prosecutors say Wanying Zhang, also know as Heather, surveilled the Taiwanese president's son and his family.

entries.title: Imran Khan supporters march in Pakistan to demand his release after talks failed
entries.snippet: Talks between Khan's party and the government failed two days ago. Besides Khan's release, protesters demand his transfer to a hospital and family visits.

entries.title: SCOTUS hears major climate change case. And, Brazil's presidential race goes to runoff
entries.snippet: The Supreme Court is set to hear a blockbuster climate change case that could affect more than just climate issues. And, Brazil's presidential race is too close to call.

entries.title: FlyDubai attacker intended to crash plane into Tel Aviv airport, ongoing investigation finds
entries.snippet: The investigation has found the attacker intended to crash the plane into Israel's Ben Gurion International Airport, a person familiar with the matter not authorized to speak publicly told NPR.

entries.title: Nobel medicine prize goes to 3 scientists for research into brain activity
entries.snippet: The Nobel Prize in medicine was awarded Monday to three scientists working on the mechanisms the brain uses to switch on, or off, the activity of individual nerve cells.

entries.title: Former Prince Andrew files legal action to quash warrants that led to residence searches
entries.snippet: A judicial spokesperson confirmed that Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor had filed a claim with the High Court in London and a hearing would take place Thursday.

entries.title: Spain's prime minister calls early elections as pressure mounts over housing crisis
entries.snippet: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez announced early elections Monday after his government suffered a bruising legislative defeat last week on emergency measures related to the country's housing crisis.

entries.title: Super El Niño is here. What's so super about it?
entries.snippet: This year, federal forecasters say the planet could see the strongest El Niño event on record. Here's what you need to know.

entries.title: Republicans and Democrats find a unifying target: Pharmacy benefit managers
entries.snippet: Republicans and Democrats, both patients and politicians, seem united in their disdain for the healthcare companies known as pharmacy benefit managers. Tennessee and Arkansas are regulating them now.

entries.title: LISTEN LIVE: Supreme Court hears case seeking damages from fossil fuel industry for climate change
entries.snippet: On Monday, the first day of the Supreme Court's new term, the justices will hear the Boulder case that could decide the fate of others like it.

entries.title: AP report: U.S. Air Force removes all bombers from British air base targeted by a suspected terror attack
entries.snippet: The U.S. Air Force has brought home its bombers stationed at a U.S.-run military air base in England used to strike Iran following an investigation into a planned terror attack at the RAF Fairford base.

entries.title: Major oil exporters agree to keep production steady in November
entries.snippet: The so-called OPEC+ subgroup — Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Algeria and Oman — will meet again on Nov. 1 to review conditions in the oil market.

entries.title: WATCH: 3 scientists win Nobel Prize in medicine for studying mysteries of the brain
entries.snippet: Karl Deisseroth, 54, Peter Hegemann, 71, and Georg Nagel, 73, have carried out research into light-gated ion channels and optogenetics.

entries.title: Despair over future fuels political anxiety for college students on the cusp of adulthood
entries.snippet: Their anxiety is fueling a restlessness with a national political system that they worry is no longer capable of improving their lives or no longer interested in helping.

entries.title: The misperception that keeps bystanders from intervening and how to short‑circuit it
entries.snippet: People may accept bad behavior — even sexual assault — when they overestimate how acceptable their peers think it is. But there are ways to undermine this thinking and make intervention more likely.

entries.title: Search ongoing for missing medical flight from Bermuda to Boston as crews plan to scour ocean floor
entries.snippet: The Federal Aviation Administration contacted the Coast Guard at 2 a.m. Saturday that it had lost contact with the Gulfstream G100 carrying four Canadians and two Bermudian nationals over the Atlantic Ocean.

entries.title: Serb separatist Dodik declares victory in Bosnia vote as ethnic tensions and EU hopes collide
entries.snippet: Around 3.4 million voters were eligible to choose the three members of the country's multi-ethnic presidency, lawmakers for the national parliament and heads of institutions for the country's two entities.

entries.title: Trump names national intelligence director Jay Clayton to lead a new federal AI task force
entries.snippet: The announcement comes after Trump hosted top executives of AI companies at the White House last week and said they had signed a voluntary accord that would effectively self-police the development of the technology.

entries.title: AP report: UAE had shared details about FlyDubai flight with Israel, including pilots' names and nationalities
entries.snippet: With the investigation underway, preliminary details about the incident have highlighted several major security lapses.

entries.title: Christa Pike's lawyer says she has not regained consciousness since her failed Tennessee execution
entries.snippet: Little has been released about Pike's condition since Wednesday night's execution attempt. She has since remained hospitalized under guard as doctors try to get the massive dose of the barbiturate pentobarbital out of her system.

entries.title: Brazilians voted for next president as Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro hope for first round victory
entries.snippet: Bolsonaro is the son of far-right former President Jair Bolsonaro and an ally of U.S. President Donald Trump. Lula is running in his seventh presidential election and has strengthened Brazil's ties with Beijing.

entries.title: Cornell president calls alleged gang rape 'deeply disturbing,' pledges greater transparency
entries.snippet: "My heart aches when I think of what she experienced," Kotlikoff said. "It raises heartbreaking and troubling issues about sexual assault, dehumanization and aspects of party culture, alcohol and drug use."

entries.title: A $28 billion hemp THC industry is fighting to save itself from a looming federal ban
entries.snippet: America's multibillion-dollar market for impairing hemp products faces potential elimination after Congress voted to close a loophole in federal law that has allowed it to flourish.

entries.title: Trump defends data centers in Ohio as he rallies to boost Jon Husted in a tight Senate race
entries.snippet: Trump is embarking on what he says will be a 32-day blitz ahead of the Nov. 3 elections, hitting the deep red states of Texas, Oklahoma and Alabama this week before pivoting to Ohio, a battleground state that's home to one of the top-tier Senate races this cycle.

entries.title: Inside the study for a remedy to fight Congo's deadliest Ebola outbreak
entries.snippet: The drug is targeted at Bundibugyo virus, which is responsible for the fast-moving outbreak and is without an approved vaccine or treatment. The trial began in July and is one of several studies launched to find some protection and another way of at least slowing the outbreak.

entries.title: What to know about the Kelvin wave raising the sea level along the West Coast
entries.snippet: Kelvin waves are not like tsunamis, and they don't curl over and crash on the beach. A better image is water sloshing in the bathtub or a swimming pool during an earthquake. In the ocean, they are bulges of water that lift the sea level as they move along the coast.

entries.title: Prosecutor says 2 Iranian men scouted a UK synagogue for a chlorine bomb plot
entries.snippet: The Heaton Park synagogue was the site of an attack on Yom Kippur, the holiest day of the Jewish calendar, on Oct. 2, 2025, when Jihad Al-Shamie crashed his car into the gates and then began a knife attack.

entries.title: A gut punch in Ohio: Nearly 1,400 laid off at truck factory just days before Trump rally
entries.snippet: This year's election is a test for the working-class coalition that lifted Trump into the White House and gave majorities to Republicans in the House and Senate.

entries.title: Suspected pneumonic plague in Siberia: What we know about the disease
entries.snippet: A worker at a plague research institute in Siberia has died, and nearly 200 of her contacts are under medical observation. Russian authorities deny a link to the bacterial infection. The US is monitoring the situation.

entries.title: Klopp's first Germany internationals: What did we learn?
entries.snippet: Jürgen Klopp has done things a little differently since becoming Germany coach. Casting a wider net for talent and trying to connect with players and country haven't make an immediate impact, but he is not bowed.

entries.title: Bosnia election: New technology might have stopped votes being cast on behalf of dead voters, but the result remains unchanged
entries.snippet: New technology has stopped votes being cast on behalf of dead or absent voters, and turnout has fallen to a record low. But it was a case of deja vu in Bosnia's elections with the same parties winning along ethnic lines.

entries.title: As rising seas threaten low-lying Pacific Islands, regional leaders call on the world to take climate more seriously
entries.snippet: For Pacific island nations, climate change is no distant threat. As seas rise, they're bringing the real-time consequences of a warming planet directly to world leaders in Tuvalu.

entries.title: German and US scientists win Nobel Prize in medicine for research on brain activity
entries.snippet: Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel won the award for discoveries that provide new insights into how we might treat blindness, depression, addiction and dementia.

entries.title: Israel's mental health crisis in the wake of Oct. 7 attacks
entries.snippet: More than a third of Israelis have shown symptoms of mental health conditions, a report found. Three years after the October 7 attack, the country's health system is still struggling to come to terms with its effects.

entries.title: Israel observes October 7 anniversary with national memorial day
entries.snippet: Israel is holding memorial ceremonies nationwide for those killed in the October 7, 2023 Hamas terror attacks and soldiers who died in the ensuing war.

entries.title: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez calls snap election
entries.snippet: The Spanish prime minister had repeatedly insisted he would serve out his four-year term, with elections scheduled for 2027. The move comes after a major defeat for his coalition's proposed housing reforms.

entries.title: Yemen launches major military operation against Houthis
entries.snippet: Yemen's internationally recognized government announced a new military offensive to retake Houthi-held territory after rebels cut a key road linking the city of Taiz with Aden.

entries.title: India news: Top court hears petitions against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar
entries.snippet: The Supreme Court heard pleas against India's beleagured poll body chief over alleged unilateral decisions related to the large-scale revision of voter lists. DW has the latest.

entries.title: Hundreds of French schools closed amid protests
entries.snippet: The student protests that rocked France last week have prompted authorities to keep up to 500 schools closed on Monday. More protests are planned for Tuesday.

entries.title: Middle East oil exports recover to pre-Iran war levels despite Hormuz attacks
entries.snippet: Gulf crude exports returned to pre-war levels in September, with producers increasingly relying on alternative routes and ship-to-ship transfers to bypass Hormuz. Iranian exports remain below the pre-war average.

entries.title: US: FBI arrests woman accused of spying for China
entries.snippet: A California woman was arrested at Los Angeles International Airport, just before departing for China, with the US officials accusing her of spying on Taiwan's president's son.

entries.title: US pulls bombers out of UK's Fairford airbase after arrests
entries.snippet: Following a suspected terrorist plot targeting the UK's Fairford airbase, the US Air Force withdrew all its B-1 planes from the site.

entries.title: Brazil election: Bolsonaro and Lula head to runoff
entries.snippet: Populist Flavio Bolsonaro has secured a thin lead over incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, but the next president of Brazil will be decided in the runoff round, according to the country’s electoral court.

entries.title: Nationalists top Bosnia-Herzegovina's divisive election
entries.snippet: Bosnia-Herzegovina's three-member presidency is set to be dominated by nationalists from the three major ethnic groups, including Zeljka ​Cvijanovic, backed by disqualified Serb secessionist leader Milorad Dodik.

entries.title: Pakistan: Imran Khan supporters demand ex-PM's release
entries.snippet: Thousands of Imran Khan supporters have begun a trek to Islamabad to demand he be freed as Pakistan's political leadership remains in deadlock. The government has set up roadblocks to keep protesters at bay.

entries.title: Anthropic report: Is Russia using AI for disinformation in the Central African Republic and elsewhere across Africa?
entries.snippet: An Anthropic report says the AI model Claude was used in pro-Russian campaigns in the Central African Republic. Similar allegations were raised for the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Kenya, Sudan and Mali.

entries.title: Germany's Merz visits Kyiv as Russia strikes bridge
entries.snippet: As air raid sirens sounded in Kyiv, Chancellor Merz called on President Putin to end his "senseless war" and announced new measures to support Ukraine, including plans for joint Ukrainian-German drone production.
